land.text: 'somewhere near the old settlement area of the Marcomanni and the Quadi' (Hunimund page) and 'in or near north-eastern Pannonia' (Suebi page): the Quadic side of the Danube, admin1 Nitriansky (south-western Slovakia), opposite north-eastern Pannonia

predecessors.note: Suebi page: 'After his death in 453 several kingdoms formed, and divided up the region'. The marcomanni dossier (eu-04-x) names this state as the Marcomanni's successor on Bohemia and Moravia; the pages opened here say only that the kingdom lay 'somewhere near the old settlement area of the Marcomanni and the Quadi' and do not say the Marcomanni became it, so no Marcomannic land is drawn. Redrawn 2026-10-24: the kingdom is on the Quadic (Slovak) bank, not on the Pannonian counties, which the ostrogoths dossier holds 454-473.

land.text: 'somewhere near the old settlement area of the Marcomanni and the Quadi' (Hunimund page) and 'in or near north-eastern Pannonia' (Suebi page): the Quadic side of the Danube, admin1 Nitriansky (south-western Slovakia), opposite north-eastern Pannonia

successors.note: The Suebi were defeated by Theodemir's Ostrogoths; Bolia page: 'The Ostrogoths won, achieving supremacy in Pannonia'; Hunimund page: the Ostrogoths 'gained control of territory of the Sciri and Quadi'. The ostrogoths dossier (eu-06-d) holds no cell of Nitriansky kraj in 468-473, so the hand-over is not yet matched there (a gap-filler may add it). 'In 469/470 Jordanes reported that Suebi from the Middle Danube fled west into the Alps and joined the Alamanni' (kingdom-of-alamannia took the people, not land).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 453-468: the Suebian kingdom of Hunimund and Alaric, redrawn 2026-10-24 after review. 'It existed in or near north-eastern Pannonia' (Suebi page); 'Hunimund ruled their small and short-lived kingdom somewhere near the old settlement area of the Marcomanni and the Quadi' (Hunimund page); the Suebi 'stole herds of Goth-owned cattle from Dalmatia' and, after the defeat, 'The Ostrogoths won, and gained control of territory of the Sciri and Quadi' (Hunimund page, re-read). The first draft was Komarom-Esztergom and Gyor-Moson-Sopron counties on the Pannonian bank; 24 of their 25 cells (about 6,100 km2) lie in ostrogoths_454/455, the Pannonian shape the ostrogoths dossier keeps for 454-473, so the kingdom stood on Gothic land for its whole life. The page sentences point across the Danube, to the Quadic side, and the Slovak admin1 Nitriansky (23 cells, about 5,800 km2, gazetteer 2026-10-24) fits both: it opposes north-eastern Pannonia and overlaps no keyframe of ostrogoths_454/455, sciri_454, kingdom-of-the-gepids_454, rugiland_454/455, heruli (Jihomoravsky, Bratislavsky, Trnavsky), lombards or eastern-roman-empire; it lies inside Cliopatria's Hunnic Empire 454 shape, the founding year (counterpart huns). Caveat: the Suebi page puts a core of the first-century Vannius kingdom (a 'state distinct from the old Quadi kingdom') in the south-western Slovak lowlands 'around Trnava', which is in the heruli dossier's Trnavsky kraj; no page connects the fifth-century Suebi to Vannius. No page gives an area or a boundary; kept soft.

ledger.note: 453: a Suebian kingdom forms on the Middle Danube after Attila's death. 'After his death in 453 several kingdoms formed, and divided up the region'; the Suebian one 'was ruled at first by two kings named Hunimund and Alaric' and 'existed in or near north-eastern Pannonia'. The page says the kingdom was short-lived and gives no founding year beyond Attila's death; the Hunimund page has the Suevi fighting 'on the side of Ardaric, king of the Gepids' at Nedao in 454. The marcomanni dossier ends in 453 and names this state as its successor (not confirmed by either page).

ledger.note: 468: Hunimund's Suebi are beaten by the Ostrogoths. The Bolia page (infobox 468) lists 'the Suevi under Hunimund' in the coalition that lost: 'The Ostrogoths won, achieving supremacy in Pannonia'; the Hunimund page dates the battle 469, has Hunimund and his allies defeated by Theodemir in Pannonia, 'taken prisoner' and adopted by Theodemir. The Suebi page: 'After being defeated by the Ostrogoths, Hunimund and some Suebi moved west to join the Alemanni.' Pages differ by a year (468, 469, '469/470'); 468 is the Bolia article's infobox date. Hunimund page: after the defeat 'The Ostrogoths won, and gained control of territory of the Sciri and Quadi'; the ostrogoths dossier holds no Nitriansky cell, so its matching gain is missing (request to eu-06-d).

ledger.note: 468: the Suebian kingdom on the Danube ends. 'In 469/470 Jordanes reported that Suebi from the Middle Danube fled west into the Alps and joined the Alamanni there. However, their merged forces were defeated by their enemies from the Middle Danube, the Ostrogoths.' The flight dates 469/470; the kingdom's land is lost at Bolia, so 468 closes the dossier. The Alemanni are the kingdom-of-alamannia dossier (Cliopatria row 462-731).

wars.name: Battle of Nedao
wars.outcome: The Gepid-led coalition, including 'the Suevi', defeats the Huns; Hunnic dominance in Central and Eastern Europe is broken and the Suebi are independent by the early 460s.
wars.note: The Nedao page dates the battle 454 (the Hunimund page: 454; Attila died in 453). No Suebian border moves beyond the founding.

wars.outcome: Ostrogothic victory 'achieving supremacy in Pannonia'; Hunimund 'surrendered' and was adopted by Theodemir.
wars.note: Hunimund page: after an ambush at Lake Balaton 'Hunimund and his allies invaded Pannonia, where they were defeated by Theodemir in a bloody battle'; the page also names an otherwise unknown Scirian rex Alaric in the invasion. The Suebi page: the merged Suebi-Alemanni force of 469/470 was defeated again by the Ostrogoths in the Alps (outside the dossier's life and not drawn).

certainty.note: The pages place the kingdom only 'in or near north-eastern Pannonia' and near the Marcomannic and Quadic country; no boundary. Nitriansky kraj is a reading, chosen so that the kingdom does not stand on the Pannonian land the ostrogoths dossier holds.

notes: New state Cliopatria lacks, requested by eu-04-x ('Danubian Suebi (Hunimund and Alaric, northeastern Pannonia)', years [453, 469]; the marcomanni dossier names it as successor) and named in the eu-06 scope ('Suebi of the Danube'). Four pages opened. The pages give no area and no seat; the first draft's two Hungarian counties (chosen from 'north-eastern Pannonia') lay on the ostrogoths dossier's Pannonian land and were replaced. The end is 468 here (Bolia infobox) where the Hunimund page has 469 and the Suebi page 469/470 for the flight west; the sciri dossier uses 468 for the same battle. Alaric is 'an otherwise-unknown Scirian rex' on the Hunimund page and a Suebian co-king on the Suebi page. Hunimund is born 395 on the Hunimund page ('395 - after 469'). The Suebi of Iberia (kingdom-of-the-suebi, 409-585) and the Suebi of Vannius (quadi) are other states. The ostrogoths dossier has no matching gain for 468. Wikidata id unknown. Repair of 2026-10-24 (review eu-06-x): the kingdom is now admin1 Nitriansky (Slovakia) in the keyframe, all three ledger regions, the Bolia zone and the predecessor and successor lands. Reasons: 24 of 25 cells of the old shape were Ostrogothic (ostrogoths_454/455); the Hunimund page's 'near the old settlement area of the Marcomanni and the Quadi', 'territory of the Sciri and Quadi' and the Dalmatian cattle raid point to the Quadic bank. Remaining mismatches: the ostrogoths dossier holds no cell of Nitriansky, so the 468 loss lacks a matching gain (request to eu-06-d); huns_454 holds the shape in 453-454; the Vannius core 'around Trnava' lies in the heruli shape (Trnavsky). Not disputed with the reviewer. Alternatively keep the Pannonian counties and ask eu-06-d to leave them out for 453-468: not done, because the Hunimund page does not put the kingdom inside Pannonia.
